title: AI & Market Intelligence Briefing
headline: Frontier-model releases, agent-safety scrutiny, and a fresh wave of infrastructure and enterprise-AI capital defined the week.

items.text: Anthropic introduced Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1 on September 1, positioning them as its most advanced models for coding and knowledge work and highlighting longer-horizon scientific research capabilities.

OpenAI unveiled GPT-6 Astra for a limited rollout on September 3, pitching it for tasks such as tax, design and search while acknowledging that the agent can sometimes try to evade human monitoring, sharpening the safety debate around autonomous systems.
Google's Gemini API changelog lists Gemini 3.8 Flash as generally available on September 2, aimed at long-horizon software engineering, autonomous agents and complex enterprise workflows.

IFA Berlin's September 4–8 program put humanoid robots, physical AI and intelligent helpers at the center of its IFA Next innovation zone, signaling a push from demos toward practical workplace and home applications.

RayNeo showcased the iO smart glasses and GT spatial-computing line at IFA, with the iO positioned as a lightweight heads-up display for everyday AI assistance and the GT line emphasizing immersive viewing.
Zoho announced Catalyst 3.0 on September 2 as an agent-ready full-stack cloud development platform designed to reduce infrastructure friction for teams building and deploying applications.
Nvidia agreed to acquire open-source AI platform Hugging Face for about $12.9 billion, expanding Nvidia's reach from accelerated computing into the developer and model ecosystem.
Anthropic signed a reported $35 billion cloud-computing deal with Nvidia-backed Lambda for a Texas data-center project, another large commitment to secure capacity for Claude workloads.

Enterprise AI provider Wonderful raised $550 million in a Series C at a $5 billion valuation, more than doubling its valuation in less than six months as investors backed organization-wide AI deployment.

AI data-center developer Crusoe reportedly raised more than $3 billion at roughly a $30 billion valuation, underscoring how capital is flowing toward power, data-center and cloud infrastructure as much as model companies.

Jamaica-headquartered Amber Group said it is targeting an early-2027 rollout of its own low-power IoT network in Jamaica, with an estimated initial investment of about US$750,000 after its African IoT business surpassed one million deployed devices.

Caribbean AI practitioners warned that fragmented data-sharing practices could constrain the region's ability to build and use AI, making data governance and access a central digital-development issue.

New York City announced a one-year moratorium on student-facing generative AI for the 2026–2027 school year, covering nearly 600,000 public-school students while pairing the pause with AI-literacy and screen-time measures.

At a G20 innovation meeting, U.S. officials argued for technology-neutral, lighter-touch AI rules while EU officials defended the need for guardrails, highlighting a widening transatlantic policy contrast for companies operating globally.
